page.layout: One page of text; running head at top; a short verse poem, then a rule, then a heading and a longer verse poem; catchword "IN" at the lower right.

l.i: Quos nec pati mundus queat fuperftites,
Nec ipfa forfan tartara ferant mortuos!
Nempe esse Vobis inferorum Ut omnium
Et mutuo Vos perdite, Inuidi, Inuidos,
Quum miserius nil esse possit Inuidis.

main_text.l: QVi mutuando de Suo nunquam Tuum,
Sed Vsque & Vsque de Tuo, Suum facit:
Cui sterile quod Natura condidit, parit:
Nunquam ferens qui metere nunquam definit:
Qui cocta, cruda, devorat, nunquam fatur:
Cui, sive sterile, sive fertile sit solum,
Fert Luna census menstruos, Sol annuos:
Vis iste quis sit nosse? Foenerator est,
Quo nulla mundo pestis est nocentior,
Quo nulla mundo pestis est frequentior.
At tu seuerus pauperum Vindex Deus,
Fac sapiat, aut raptus tribunal ad tuum,

page.notes: Printed page with a decorative rule between the two poems; the large initial Q of the second poem is set as a woodcut-style letter. Some letters in the first poem (e.g. "Vos", "Ut") are printed in the source as long-s/u forms and are transcribed as printed in the scan; the word "Inuidos" and "Inuidis" are as printed. Marginal ink marks and show-through were omitted.
